proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local argument, not quoted source text. Its sole long literature proof dependency is Lemma 3.3 for N>=2, whose exact matrices and Appendix A proof map are recorded in source-proof. No external lead is used. First, the smooth convex inequality used in (3.2) follows directly as follows. Integration of the L-Lipschitz gradient on a segment gives f(z)<=f(x)+<grad f(x),z-x>+(L/2)||z-x||^2. For a fixed y, the convex L-smooth function F(z)=f(z)-<grad f(y),z> is minimized at y. Apply this descent inequality to F at x with z=x-grad F(x)/L. Since F(y)<=F(z), obtain ||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2/(2L)<=f(x)-f(y)-<grad f(y),x-y>. Let r=||x*-x0||. If r=0, grad f(x0)=0 and every GM iterate equals x*, proving the bound. Otherwise set nu=(x*-x0)/r, g_i=grad f(x_i)/(Lr), delta_i=(f(x_i)-f*)/(Lr^2), i=0,...,N. Then ||nu||=1 and x_i=x0-hr sum_(j<i)g_j. For i=1,...,N, apply the preceding inequality with x=x_(i-1),y=x_i; it gives (1/2)||g_(i-1)-g_i||^2+h<g_i,g_(i-1)><=delta_(i-1)-delta_i. Applying it with x=x*,y=x_i gives (1/2)||g_i||^2+h sum_(j<i)<g_i,g_j>+<nu,g_i><=-delta_i for every i=0,...,N. These are exactly the retained (G') constraints for the actual trajectory, without needing equality of r and R or an attained worst instance. Let u_i be the coordinate vector indexed i in R^(N+1), and let G have row i equal to g_i^T. Put A_(i-1,i)=(1/2)(u_(i-1)-u_i)(u_(i-1)-u_i)^T+(h/2)(u_i u_(i-1)^T+u_(i-1)u_i^T), and D_i=(1/2)u_i u_i^T+(h/2)sum_(j<i)(u_i u_j^T+u_j u_i^T). For any nonnegative lambda_1,...,lambda_N with lambda_(i+1)>=lambda_i and lambda_N<=1, set tau_0=lambda_1, tau_i=lambda_(i+1)-lambda_i for 1<=i<N, and tau_N=1-lambda_N. Thus tau>=0, sum tau_i=1, and coefficients of all delta_i cancel in -delta_N+sum_i lambda_i(delta_i-delta_(i-1))+sum_i tau_i delta_i. Multiplying the feasible inequalities by these nonnegative multipliers gives tr(G^T QG)+tau^T G nu<=-delta_N, where Q=sum_(i=1)^N lambda_i A_(i-1,i)+sum_(i=0)^N tau_i D_i. If B=[[Q,tau/2],[tau^T/2,t/2]] is PSD, apply its quadratic form to the vector (G_:k,nu_k) for each coordinate k and sum. This yields tr(G^T QG)+tau^T G nu+(t/2)||nu||^2>=0, hence delta_N<=t/2. This establishes weak duality directly for every G and every dimension; rank-one reduction, strong duality and existence of an optimizer are unnecessary. It also fixes the p11 scalar condition: w^T Qw+tau^T w>=-t/2 for all w, not <=. The equivalence with B PSD follows because the quadratic form at (w,1) is nonnegative; for last coordinate s!=0 use homogeneity and w/s, and for s=0 pass to the limit s->0. For the normalized optimization notation, writing v=sup delta_N over the common feasible set gives val(G')=LR^2 v and val(G'')=inf(-delta_N)=-v=-val(G')/(LR^2). Thus the corrected objective scaling is exact. To exhibit the required certificate, now fix lambda_i=i/(2N+1-i), t=1/c, c=2Nh+1. The multipliers obey the above conditions, since lambda_i-lambda_(i-1)=(2N+1)/[(2N+1-i)(2N+2-i)]>0 with lambda_0=0, and lambda_N=N/(N+1)<1. Define S0,S1 indexed 0,...,N by diagonal (2lambda_1,...,2lambda_N,1). S0 has adjacent off-diagonal (S0)_(i-1,i)=-lambda_i and other off-diagonals zero. S1 has (S1)_(i,j)=tau_j for i<j and is symmetric. Directly from A,D, 2Q=M=(1-h)S0+hS1: its diagonal is as stated; for i<j its off-diagonal is h tau_j minus (1-h)lambda_j if j=i+1, and h tau_j otherwise. By source Lemma 3.3, S0,S1 are positive definite for N>=2. For N=1, they are explicitly [[1,-1/2],[-1/2,1]] and [[1,1/2],[1/2,1]], both with positive leading minors 1 and 3/4. Therefore M is positive definite for every N>=1 and 0<h<=1. Let e be the all-ones vector. From the entries, S0 e=tau. For i<N, (S1 e)_i=1+lambda_(i+1)+i tau_i=(2N+1)tau_i, using tau_i=(2N+1)/[(2N-i)(2N+1-i)] (also valid at i=0); at i=N the row sum is 1+N tau_N=(2N+1)tau_N. Hence M e=c tau and e^T M e=c, because e^T tau=1. For any v in R^(N+1) and s in R, v^T Mv+2s tau^T v+s^2/c=(v+s e/c)^T M(v+s e/c)>=0. Thus [[M,tau],[tau^T,1/c]]=2B is PSD. The direct weak-duality inequality above gives delta_N<=1/(2c). Restoring scale, f(x_N)-f*<=Lr^2/[2(2Nh+1)]<=LR^2/(4Nh+2). This proves the stated bound under the source-linked Lemma 3.3 dependency and supplies every local correction and transfer step. It does not independently reprove the long Appendix A determinant computation.

assumptions: There exists a minimizer x* with ||x0-x*||<=R.
The gradient is exact and h is fixed with 0<h<=1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^d; f:R^d->R is convex, C^1 and globally L-smooth; f*=f(x*) at a minimizer. GM is x_(i+1)=x_i-(h/L)grad f(x_i), i=0,...,N-1.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every L,R>0, positive integers d,N, h in (0,1], and every f,x0 satisfying these assumptions, the source asserts the displayed bound. Entirely deterministic.
